title: Frictionless Probe - pocket PRD + experiments
notes:
Context: quick personal sketch for a low-friction 'probe' primitive we can drop into live traffic (opt-in SDK + control-plane) to continuously check prompt-output quality and model drift without impacting end-user latency or cost targets. Goal is to surface regressions early and provide a concrete lightweight rollback signal for rollouts and canaries.

Problem statement: our current canary/rollout signal is mainly perf and error-rate (timeouts, OOMs). We catch quality regressions late (user complaints, evals). Need a lightweight synthetic quality probe that:
- runs on a tiny percent of requests or in background pre-warming flows
- is privacy-conscious (no PII collection; local redact or hashed checks)
- has ~0 added latency to user-facing requests (prefer background or shadowing)
- cheap: micro-prompts, short context, small model variants for checks
- produces actionable metrics (semantic drift score, hallucination spike, style/regression tags)

Core idea / shape:
- SDK + server-side controller. SDK tags a subset of requests as "probe-eligible" (sampling rules: percent-of-users, percent-of-routes, session-based). For each eligible event, the SDK either (A) sends a tiny parallel probe request to a probe model (shadow), or (B) constructs a compact synthetic prompt (summary + question) and schedules a probe run to a cheap model asynchronously.
- Controller collects probe outputs, computes lightweight signals (BLEU-ish is not enough; use embedding-similarity to baseline + heuristic checks), surfaces alerts in Console (per-route) and feeds into rollout gating.
- Privacy: probe prompts are derived: either template + hashed user-id OR local redact and summary hashing. Default OFF for enterprise customers; opt-in for Hosted by default but with clear privacy UI.

User stories (rough):
- As an engineering PM, I want a daily drift chart per-route so I can tell when a new model rollout changes tone or correctness.
- As SRE, I want probe runs to never increase p50 latency; probes must be async/shadowed or run on separate lightweight pool.
- As platform engineer, I want an abort rule: if probe semantic-similarity drops below threshold for N minutes, automatically rollback canary.
- As privacy officer, I want all probe payloads to be redacted and stored only for 7 days unless explicitly flagged for debugging.

Experiment matrix / metrics to capture:
- Sampling strategy: 0.1%, 0.5%, 1% of routed requests vs per-session seed sampling
- Probe model variants: same model (baseline) vs smaller quantized model (fast) vs deterministic reranker
- Metrics: embedding cosine to golden set, hallucination heuristics (presence of unsupported facts), style shift (sentence length, sentiment shift), token-delta distribution, alert precision/recall vs human labeler
- Cost impact: tokens consumed, additional compute (GPU-seconds) per 1k user requests
- Latency impact: measure p50/p95 end-to-end with and without probe enabled on shadow path

Alerting/UX:
- Console: per-route drift timeline, last offending probe examples (redacted), confidence score, suggested remediation (rollback, tweak prompt, increase model size)
- Slack/webhook: threshold-based alerts with short digest and link to quick rollback
- Debug mode: allow retention of raw probe payloads for 30 days for incident triage (explicit enterprise opt-in)

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: SDK local-only probe run on dev clusters, use synthetic traffic and a small set of routes (search, summarize) — 2 weeks
2) Small beta (hosted internal customers): enable background probes on 1% of sessions, probe model = tiny quantized variant, surface in Console — 4 weeks
3) Public beta: opt-in customers can enable per-route probes; add automatic canary gating (rollback on sustained drop) — 6–8 weeks
4) Enterprise opt-in with KMS redaction controls and audit logs — post-beta

Open questions / TODOs:
- Baseline creation: how to maintain per-route golden examples? Manual curation vs auto-seed from last known-good model.
- Metric calibration: what thresholds map to actionable rollbacks? Need human-labeled ground truth.
- Cost tradeoffs: is async probe to cheap model sufficient or do we need to shadow full model for fidelity? Estimate cost multiplier.
- UX: What is the best way to present "probing" to customers and get consent? Can we piggyback on current data-retention/consent flows?
- Failure modes: too many false positives -> rollback churn; how to dampen via hysteresis and ensemble signals.

Quick next steps (personal):
- Spike: implement probe SDK hook that samples and sends a compact probe to a local tiny model, compute embedding-sim and send to local dashboard (1 week)
- Write short Confluence page that defines metric prototypes and labeling rubric (pair with Mika) (2 days)
- Sync with Evan for cost/infra implications and pool design (30m)

Random ideas / fringe: 'probe ghosts' where we run off-line historical request replay as continuous backfill for drift scoring; 'probe contracts' where customers specify which routes are probe-eligible and which portions of payload are allowed in probes; per-tenant thresholds (some customers are noise-tolerant).

Notes to self: keep this mini-PRD under 1 page for leadership; companion doc = implementation checklist + infra cost table. Don't bake privacy-insecure shortcuts.

-- sofia
